conventions.convention: Momenta lie in C⁴; h(p,q)=p⁰q⁰−p¹q¹−p²q²−p³q³=−η(p,q), with η=diag(−1,1,1,1). The Pauli map is κ(p)=p⁰I₂+Σpʲσⱼ. Dotted and undotted spinors are independent complex vectors.

Spinor factors are nonzero and identified by (λ,λ̃)↦(tλ,t⁻¹λ̃), t∈C×. Both alternating tensors have ε¹²=1 and ε²¹=−1; indices are raised with these tensors. A helicity-h amplitude scales as t^(−2h) on each leg.

The dimensionless shift is λᵢ(z)=λᵢ+zλⱼ and λ̃ⱼ(z)=λ̃ⱼ−zλ̃ᵢ. Residues are coefficients of (z−zα)⁻¹. Rationality, regularity at zero, distinct simple nonzero finite poles, decay at infinity, and channel residue factorization are explicit hypotheses.

Polarization vectors use the inverse raised-index Pauli map. Reference denominators must be nonzero; pure gauge means a vector difference proportional to p. Reference-independent contraction requires the complex-bilinear condition h(p,J)=0.
The residue at infinity is minus the coefficient of z⁻¹ in the Laurent expansion there; the boundary correction is −Res∞(A(z)/z).

load_bearing.statement: A spinor factorization of a rank-one matrix M is a pair of nonzero two-spinors satisfying Mₐₐ̇=λₐλ̃ₐ̇; its spinor-helicity class is the equivalence class under (λ,λ̃)↦(tλ,t⁻¹λ̃), t∈C×.
For every p∈C⁴, det κ(p)=h(p,p). Every nonzero null p has a spinor factorization; any two factorizations differ by a unique rescaling (λ,λ̃)↦(tλ,t⁻¹λ̃), t∈C×.

For rational A regular at zero, with only distinct simple finite poles zα≠0 and A(z)→0 at infinity, A(0)=−Σα rα/zα=−Σα Res(z=zα)(A(z)/z). Under the stated channel residue-factorization hypothesis, substitute rα=(Σs A_L,s(zα)A_R,−s(zα))/Q′α(zα).

published_dependencies.used_for: The spinor-helicity definition cites its Pauli matrices, fixed η=diag(−1,1,1,1) convention, effective form −η, and inverse-length momentum units. The consuming definition explicitly restates the needed data.
